source_refs.note: Section 14.2 heading (PDF 17); the section has no text of its own before 14.2.1, so this topic introduces the two mechanisms described in 14.2.1 and the hormonal section.

blocks.text: The kidneys can make urine that is more concentrated or more dilute than the blood. When the body needs to save water they excrete hypertonic urine; when there is much water in the body they excrete hypotonic urine.

Two mechanisms control this: the counter-current mechanism of the loop of Henle (14.2.1), which keeps the medulla salty, and hormones, ADH and aldosterone (the next topic), which adjust how much water and salt the distal tubule and collecting duct take back.

blocks.prompt: Which two mechanisms let the kidney change the concentration of urine?
blocks.explanation: The counter-current mechanism, which keeps a high salt concentration round the loop of Henle and collecting duct, and hormonal control by ADH and aldosterone.

items: Hypertonic urine saves water; hypotonic urine removes extra water; controlled by the counter-current mechanism and by ADH and aldosterone.
